First, recall that:

- The cross product distributes over addition/subtraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}(a\pm b)\times c & =a\times c\pm b\times c \\ c\times (a\pm b) & =c\times a\pm c\times b\end{aligned}
$$

- The cross product is associative with respect to scalar multiplication:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\lambda a)\times b & =\lambda (a\times b) \\ a\times (\lambda b) & =\lambda (a\times b)\end{aligned}
$$

- The cross product of parallel vectors equals the zero vector. In particular,

$$
a\times a=0.
$$

- The cross product is anticommutative:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\times b & =-b\times a\end{aligned}
$$

With that in mind, let's evaluate our expression:

- First, we use the distributive property:

$$
\begin{aligned}(3b-c)\times (9a-2b) & = \\ ((3b)\times (9a))-((3b)\times (2b))-(c\times (9a))+(c\times (2b))\end{aligned}
$$

- Next, we factor out the scalars:

$$
\begin{aligned}(3b-c)\times (9a-2b) & = \\ ((3b)\times (9a))-((3b)\times (2b))-(c\times (9a))+(c\times (2b)) & = \\ (3\cdot 9)(b\times a)-(3\cdot 2)(b\times b)-9(c\times a)+2(c\times b) & = \\ 27(b\times a)-6(b\times b)-9(c\times a)+2(c\times b)\end{aligned}
$$

- Then, we use anticommutativity, and the fact that $b\times b=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}27(b\times a)-6(b\times b)-9(c\times a)+2(c\times b) & = \\ -27(a\times b)-6(0)+9(a\times c)+2(c\times b) & = \\ -27(a\times b)+9(a\times c)+2(c\times b)\end{aligned}
$$

- Finally, we substitute the given values and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}-27(a\times b)+9(a\times c)+2(c\times b) & = \\ -27⟨0,0,1⟩+9⟨0,-1,3⟩+2⟨0,2,0⟩ & = \\ ⟨0,0,-27⟩+⟨0,-9,27⟩+⟨0,4,0⟩ & = \\ ⟨0,-5,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

First, recall that:

  • The cross product distributes over addition/subtraction: (a±b)×c=a×c±b×cc×(a±b)=c×a±c×b

  • The cross product is associative with respect to scalar multiplication: (λa)×b=λ(a×b)a×(λb)=λ(a×b)

  • The cross product of parallel vectors equals the zero vector. In particular, a×a=0.

  • The cross product is anticommutative: a×b=−b×a

With that in mind, let's evaluate our expression:

  • First, we use the distributive property: (3b−c)×(9a−2b)=((3b)×(9a))−((3b)×(2b))−(c×(9a))+(c×(2b))

  • Next, we factor out the scalars: (3b−c)×(9a−2b)=((3b)×(9a))−((3b)×(2b))−(c×(9a))+(c×(2b))=(3⋅9)(b×a)−(3⋅2)(b×b)−9(c×a)+2(c×b)=27(b×a)−6(b×b)−9(c×a)+2(c×b)

  • Then, we use anticommutativity, and the fact that b×b=0: 27(b×a)−6(b×b)−9(c×a)+2(c×b)=−27(a×b)−6(0)+9(a×c)+2(c×b)=−27(a×b)+9(a×c)+2(c×b)

  • Finally, we substitute the given values and simplify: −27(a×b)+9(a×c)+2(c×b)=−27⟨0,0,1⟩+9⟨0,−1,3⟩+2⟨0,2,0⟩=⟨0,0,−27⟩+⟨0,−9,27⟩+⟨0,4,0⟩=⟨0,−5,0⟩
